text.en: The Waste Warriors look for litter and count the dustbins in the school. They find out whether students use them.

We can reduce waste by using only what we need, reusing things and not throwing away useful items.
Some waste, like food peels, leftovers and paper, still remains. We separate waste into dry waste and wet waste to manage it better.
Old newspapers are never thrown into bins. They are given to traditional recyclers. Different recyclers collect different items.
Find out what your school gives to the recycler and what recyclers do. Ask a recycler to visit your class. Recyclers and sanitation workers do important work and deserve respect.
Play the segregation game: make 30 to 40 chits of items, put them in boxes labelled green for wet waste, blue for dry waste and a third for recycler items.
Trees give shade, keep the air clean and are home to birds and insects. Under a tree the temperature is lower than in the Sun.
Fire safety: move calmly to the nearest exit, crawl low under smoke with your mouth covered, do not hide in closets, go to the assembly point and report if anyone is missing. Never go back into the building.
Traffic safety: follow the traffic rules and design a signboard for the school gate.

problem.en: Sort these: banana peel, old newspaper, vegetable scraps, plastic bottle.

text.en: Banana peel and vegetable scraps are wet waste.
Newspaper and plastic bottle are dry waste.
Give dry items to the recycler.

prompt.en: How do we keep our school clean and safe?

points.en: Know fire and traffic safety rules.
